summary: This bill bars registered sex offenders from entering or receiving services from any domestic violence or homeless shelter that gets federal funds, makes violating shelters ineligible for such funds the next year, and imposes fines or up to 5 years in prison on offenders who knowingly enter anyway.

scores.thoughts: The bill conditions federal funding eligibility on shelters' compliance with the prohibition on serving covered sex offenders. Non-compliant shelters lose access to federal funds in the following fiscal year. This creates a spending-related enforcement mechanism but does not expand or broadly reduce overall government spending levels; the effect is narrow and conditional.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or tax policy.
The bill addresses domestic violence and homeless shelters but does not engage with healthcare systems, coverage, or delivery models.
The bill has no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill has no provisions related to immigration, borders, or pathways for non-citizens.
The bill has no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill has no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill has no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.

The bill directly regulates access to federally funded homeless shelters and domestic violence shelters (core components of the social safety net) by barring covered sex offenders. This imposes eligibility restrictions on safety-net services rather than expanding them.
The bill has no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill has no provisions related to drugs, decriminalization, or enforcement.

The bill adds a new federal criminal penalty (fine and/or up to 5 years imprisonment) for covered sex offenders who knowingly enter or use prohibited shelters and fail to notify staff of their registry status. This constitutes an additional punitive measure aimed at a specific class of offenders.
The bill has no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill has no provisions addressing deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill has no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill has no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill has no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill has no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
The bill has no provisions related to labor, unions, or worker protections.
The bill has no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
